response: {"headline": "REVEAL met its primary endpoint for major coronary events with anacetrapib, a narrow success driven by LDL-C lowering rather than the intended HDL-C raising mechanism.", "summary": "The REVEAL trial (30,449 participants with vascular disease, 4.1-year median follow-up) met its primary endpoint of major coronary events (coronary death, MI, or coronary revascularization) per the Merck announcement on June 27, 2017. The calculator predicted success with 67% probability based on a 0.626 mmol/L LDL-C equivalent reduction (expected HR 0.871, 12.9% RRR), though power was only 67% at the stringent alpha=0.01 (MDE for 80% power HR 0.855). The design assumed 15% RRR with 88% power. The intended biomarker HDL-C increased 118% (A Multiregional, Randomized Evaluation...) to 138% (REVEAL trial design paper), but CETP genetics (score 0.736) indicate benefit is mediated through LDL-C lowering, not HDL-C raising. No off-target safety signals emerged.
